title: USDA announces $25 million sterile fly facility and Douglas Port reopening in Arizona
text:
USDA announces $25 million sterile fly facility and Douglas Port reopening in Arizona
M. K. Barron
Representative Juan Ciscomani joined U.S. Secretary of Agriculture Brooke Rollins in Douglas as the U.S. Department of Agriculture announced on July 29 a $25 million investment to reestablish a sterile fly dispersal facility and the reopening of the Douglas Port of Entry in Southern Arizona. The measures are intended to safely resume cattle imports from Sonora while strengthening national biosecurity against the New World screwworm threat.
The announcements came during Secretary Rollins’ second visit to Arizona’s Sixth Congressional District this year, underscoring continued collaboration with Southern Arizona’s agricultural community. "I was proud to join Secretary Rollins for today’s announcement of the reopening of the Douglas Port of Entry alongside this critical investment in Arizona," said Representative Ciscomani. "Local agriculture leaders and I have been fighting to deliver this sterile fly dispersal facility because Arizona’s livestock industry cannot afford to wait on the New World screwworm threat. This $25 million investment is the direct result of that work, and I’m grateful to Secretary Rollins for listening to Arizona’s producers and delivering on it. Her responsiveness and willingness to act swiftly on commonsense solutions has made a real difference. This is Secretary Rollins' second visit to Arizona in just a few months, reflecting her commitment to hearing directly from those on the ground and delivering real results for our farmers, ranchers, and rural communities."
Earlier this month, Ciscomani also supported the University of Arizona's successful application for a $3.74 million USDA New World Screwworm Grand Challenge Grant aimed at expanding research, surveillance, education, outreach, and developing detection technologies related to screwworm preparedness.
Ciscomani has worked closely with federal officials and local producers advocating for science-based solutions such as domestic sterile fly dispersal facilities as part of long-term efforts against New World screwworms.
John Ladd, President of Cochise-Graham Cattle Growers Association, said: "And after today, let's go for it. This is what we need to do. And this has been a really good example of all of the representative, senators, and secretaries of how it works when you have quality people and I'm proud to be here. Thank you." The USDA's announcements build upon longstanding advocacy supporting research investments in biosecurity while promoting lawful trade between Mexico and the United States.
Juan Ciscomani currently serves in Congress representing Arizona's 6th district after replacing Ann Kirkpatrick in 2023; he was born in Hermosillo, Mexico in 1982 before moving to Tucson where he resides now; he graduated from University of Arizona with a BA in 2005, according to Representative Juan Ciscomani's office.
